items: The page reads through yesterday: today's orders are still arriving.
Ad spend, clicks and paid traffic are loaded once a week, so the latest days may have none yet; plan comparisons for those metrics undercount the last days.
Rates (conversion, ROAS, CPC, completion, net margin) are computed by OWOX for the whole period, never averaged across months.
A period's plan is the sum of the plan's days in it. A rate's plan is the ratio of planned sums, as each [Plan] Data Mart's description says.
Store ROAS matches spend to the orders of the sessions it bought. The platforms' own claim (Platform ROAS in Unified Ad Spend) runs about a third higher.
Head of Marketing has no plan: its platform reports live in four warehouses, so no single query reaches all of them. Its tab shows margin against each category's target margin.

improvements.text: Finance plans the settled share (settled ÷ booked revenue), but no field holds it. Add a calculated field Settled Share to Purchases: the Finance tab then shows its critical number against [Plan] Finance.

Sales plans average order value, but it spans Purchases and Orders. Add a calculated field Average Order Value to Purchases (settled revenue ÷ distinct orders): the Sales tab then shows it against plan.
The [Plan] Data Marts store the date as text, so they cannot be joined to the facts. A date field lets every plan join to its fact by day.
Head of Marketing has no plan. A plan for spend by platform, or a target for net margin, gives that tab plan vs fact and status.
